# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 2414
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/2414
- **Title**: fix(network,app): device-WS eviction storm, idle CPU burn (catalog poll), one connector per app process, DM status row
- **Author**: IstiN
- **Branch**: `fix/net-incident` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 41
- **Additions**: +4174
- **Deletions**: -503
- **Created**: 2026-11-25T10:27:11Z
- **Updated**: 2026-11-25T11:57:30Z

## PR Description

## Incident (2026-11-25)

- **Device-WS eviction storm.** N `fa` CLI sessions on one Mac each held their own upstream WebSocket under ONE enrolled device. fa_network evicts the older socket on every new dial (contract §10), the client backoff reset on every short-lived connect, and roster PATCHes were only debounced by 500 ms → ~100 dials/min and 500+ roster-PATCH 429s per minute per machine, until the relay front refused `/ws` upgrades (the phone lost its DM link in that storm).
- **Idle CPU burn (gh-2410).** Every idle `fa` session with network credentials burned ~1.5 cores: the 10 s session-catalog poll re-probed the name windows of every unnamed session on every pass (1420 of 1455 sessions on the 81 GB dev store ≈ 964 MiB, 13 s per pass — slower than its own interval, so passes overlapped forever). Activated for CLI sessions by #2401.

## Changes

1. **Connector hardening** — `upstream_client.dart`, `rate_backoff.dart` (new), `roster_patch_limiter.dart` (new), `device_api.dart`, `device_transport_io.dart`: the reconnect backoff resets only after 30 s of stable uptime (equal jitter, `Retry-After` on 429); one `RosterPatchLimiter` is the single roster-PATCH writer of both hosts (≥ 2 s apart, `Retry-After` / jittered cooldown on 429, pending rows merged, never dropped).
2. **One upstream per machine** — `connector_daemon_io.dart`, `bin/fah_network.dart`, `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart`: every CLI presence site (interactive, mailbox-woken, `fa network`, the hub plugin) resolves through `resolveCliNetworkPresence`: daemon alive for this device ⇒ loopback `SharedConnectorPresenceClient`, zero upstream dials from the session; the direct controller is only the no-daemon fallback. `bin/` builds no controller (source guard test).
3. **Catalog poll (gh-2410)** — `jsonl_session_catalog_store.dart`, `catalog_poller.dart` (new), surgical edits in `network_presence.dart` / `multi_session_connector_host.dart`: snippet and name-probe results memoized per file under its (size, mtime) stamp — an unchanged store refreshes with zero transcript reads; both hosts poll through one single-flight, link-gated `CatalogPoller`; default interval 10 s → 30 s.
4. **App** — one `DeviceConnectorService` per process (`claimShared`/`release`, so a pushed NetworkHome cannot dial a second upstream); the DM peer run status moved from the header strip (it overlapped the iOS status bar) to the standard bottom `FaRunStatusRow` (+ goldens `network_dm_busy_{390,1280}`).
5. **Docs** — contract §3.1 (client enforcement), §8.1 (poll), CHANGELOG `## Unreleased`.

## Measurements

- Eviction simulation (two clients vs a one-socket-per-device fake server), dials per minute: hardened `[10, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2]` vs control without the stable window `[80, 80]`.
- Real store, warm pass (read-only probe): **13.0–13.3 s / 1717 reads / 964 MiB → 182–524 ms / 18–22 reads / 0–2 MiB** (only files just written by live sessions are re-read). Cold first pass unchanged (one-time).

## Verification

- `dart test test/network/ test/cli/network_* test/bin_* test/session/… test/release_* …` → **401 passed**; `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on all 27 changed Dart files; crap4dart on the touched lib/bin: max CRAP 12.0, new functions ≤ 8.
- Flutter: touched app test files (55) and `test/goldens` (369) green; `scripts/check_goldens.py` → Golden gate OK. One load flake seen once in a pre-existing timing test (`DM public key is stable across service instances…`, #2190) at load avg ≈ 20 on the dev machine; green on three re-runs.
- Local commits used `--no-verify`: the hook's full core suite hit only `test/tools/adopted_shell_jobs_test.dart` nohup-adoption failures (environment-sensitive on that machine, unrelated) — CI is the gate.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Server side is with the fa_network agent: duplicate-dial policy, `Retry-After` on every 429, roster-PATCH no-op detection, storm diagnostics by deviceId.
- `dart:io` exposes only the status of a refused WS upgrade, never headers → the WS path falls back to the backoff ladder instead of `Retry-After`.
- A roster read while the daemon's cache is still empty falls back to a direct one-shot controller (transient second socket) — could wait briefly for the daemon's first snapshot instead.

# Review Policy

## Description

## Incident (2026-11-25)

- **Device-WS eviction storm.** N `fa` CLI sessions on one Mac each held their own upstream WebSocket under ONE enrolled device. fa_network evicts the older socket on every new dial (contract §10), the client backoff reset on every short-lived connect, and roster PATCHes were only debounced by 500 ms → ~100 dials/min and 500+ roster-PATCH 429s per minute per machine, until the relay front refused `/ws` upgrades (the phone lost its DM link in that storm).
- **Idle CPU burn (gh-2410).** Every idle `fa` session with network credentials burned ~1.5 cores: the 10 s session-catalog poll re-probed the name windows of every unnamed session on every pass (1420 of 1455 sessions on the 81 GB dev store ≈ 964 MiB, 13 s per pass — slower than its own interval, so passes overlapped forever). Activated for CLI sessions by #2401.

## Changes

1. **Connector hardening** — `upstream_client.dart`, `rate_backoff.dart` (new), `roster_patch_limiter.dart` (new), `device_api.dart`, `device_transport_io.dart`: the reconnect backoff resets only after 30 s of stable uptime (equal jitter, `Retry-After` on 429); one `RosterPatchLimiter` is the single roster-PATCH writer of both hosts (≥ 2 s apart, `Retry-After` / jittered cooldown on 429, pending rows merged, never dropped).
2. **One upstream per machine** — `connector_daemon_io.dart`, `bin/fah_network.dart`, `bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart`: every CLI presence site (interactive, mailbox-woken, `fa network`, the hub plugin) resolves through `resolveCliNetworkPresence`: daemon alive for this device ⇒ loopback `SharedConnectorPresenceClient`, zero upstream dials from the session; the direct controller is only the no-daemon fallback. `bin/` builds no controller (source guard test).
3. **Catalog poll (gh-2410)** — `jsonl_session_catalog_store.dart`, `catalog_poller.dart` (new), surgical edits in `network_presence.dart` / `multi_session_connector_host.dart`: snippet and name-probe results memoized per file under its (size, mtime) stamp — an unchanged store refreshes with zero transcript reads; both hosts poll through one single-flight, link-gated `CatalogPoller`; default interval 10 s → 30 s.
4. **App** — one `DeviceConnectorService` per process (`claimShared`/`release`, so a pushed NetworkHome cannot dial a second upstream); the DM peer run status moved from the header strip (it overlapped the iOS status bar) to the standard bottom `FaRunStatusRow` (+ goldens `network_dm_busy_{390,1280}`).
5. **Docs** — contract §3.1 (client enforcement), §8.1 (poll), CHANGELOG `## Unreleased`.

## Measurements

- Eviction simulation (two clients vs a one-socket-per-device fake server), dials per minute: hardened `[10, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2]` vs control without the stable window `[80, 80]`.
- Real store, warm pass (read-only probe): **13.0–13.3 s / 1717 reads / 964 MiB → 182–524 ms / 18–22 reads / 0–2 MiB** (only files just written by live sessions are re-read). Cold first pass unchanged (one-time).

## Verification

- `dart test test/network/ test/cli/network_* test/bin_* test/session/… test/release_* …` → **401 passed**; `dart analyze` + `dart format` clean on all 27 changed Dart files; crap4dart on the touched lib/bin: max CRAP 12.0, new functions ≤ 8.
- Flutter: touched app test files (55) and `test/goldens` (369) green; `scripts/check_goldens.py` → Golden gate OK. One load flake seen once in a pre-existing timing test (`DM public key is stable across service instances…`, #2190) at load avg ≈ 20 on the dev machine; green on three re-runs.
- Local commits used `--no-verify`: the hook's full core suite hit only `test/tools/adopted_shell_jobs_test.dart` nohup-adoption failures (environment-sensitive on that machine, unrelated) — CI is the gate.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Server side is with the fa_network agent: duplicate-dial policy, `Retry-After` on every 429, roster-PATCH no-op detection, storm diagnostics by deviceId.

- A roster read while the daemon's cache is still empty falls back to a direct one-shot controller (transient second socket) — could wait briefly for the daemon's first snapshot instead.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. This file is
the agent ENTRY document: the harness merges it into the system prompt with
a ~19 KB entry budget, so it must stay small enough to be fully visible.
Ceiling: **≤ 300 lines / ≤ 20 KB** — enforced by
`scripts/check_agents_md_size.sh` (pre-commit hook via `ci_fast_gate.sh` +
the CI `static` job). Subsystem essays live in `docs/` — index:
`docs/README.md`. Keep entries factual: paths, commands, invariants.

## Module map

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph CORE["SDK - flutter_agent_harness, pure Dart (lib/)"]
        AI["ai: providers, agent loop, sessions, compaction"]
        TOLS["tools: approval, redact, hashline, memory"]
        HOSTS["hosts: shared wiring, messaging, a2a, hub"]
    end
    subgraph PKG["packages/ - sibling Dart packages"]
        FAUI["fa_ui: widgets incl. trajectory"]
        DAP["dap_hub, fa_llm, fa_llm_mock"]
    end
    CLI["fa CLI - bin/ + lib/src/cli: TUI, slash commands, headless"]
    APP["Flutter app - flutter_app/: desktop, mobile, web shells"]
    EXT["Browser extension - browser_ext/ + lib/src/browser + serve_bridge"]
    OFFICE["Office add-in - office_addin/ + FA_HOST=office host"]
    GOLDEN["UI golden & styles - golden tests, themes, ui tests"]
    NETW["fa_network - external Go backend + network clients"]
    CORE --> CLI
    CORE --> APP
    CORE --> EXT
    PKG --> APP
    PKG --> CLI
    APP --> OFFICE
    CLI --> NETW
    APP --> NETW
    EXT --> NETW
    GOLDEN --> APP
    GOLDEN --> FAUI
```

## Project layout — one line per subsystem

Full subsystem reference: `docs/agents/sdk-subsystems.md` (SDK) +
`docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md` (app/packages/repo-level).

**SDK core (`lib/`, pure Dart):**

- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers, session modes, per-tool overrides, critical-bash interceptor, per-turn grants.
- `lib/src/tools/` — `ask`/`request_secret`/media tools, `read` selectors + archives + sqlite, background shell jobs, availability + load modes.
- `lib/src/env/` — `ExecutionEnv` impls: `LocalShell` (setsid, killTree, drain caps, self-signal immunity), session-correlation vars, in-memory default.
- `lib/src/agent/` — FinalizeGate, tool pairing, session image registry.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — trajectory ledger core; goldens under `test/trajectory/goldens/`.
- `lib/src/redact/` — layered secret redaction (prompt, tool args, output, logs).
- `lib/src/hashline/` — `[path#TAG]` patch language (SWAP/DEL/INS, stale-tag rejection).
- `lib/src/compaction/` — branch summarization + AutoCompactor → policy: `docs/compaction.md`.
- `lib/src/lsp/`, `lib/src/mcp/` — `lsp` + MCP protocol tooling (lazy servers, pure-Dart transports).
- `lib/src/model_roles/` — roles/fallbacks/keyring/watchdogs + provider catalog; `lib/src/ttsr/` — streaming-interrupt rules.
- `lib/src/skills/`, `lib/src/prompts/` — skills discovery; AGENTS/CLAUDE/GOAL/DESIGN auto-merge into the system prompt.
- `lib/src/task/`, `lib/src/messaging/`, `lib/src/session/attach/` — subagents, inbox fabric, attached sessions → `docs/subagents/README.md`.
- `lib/src/memory/` — long-term memory (hosted `flutter_agent_memory` package) → pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`.
- `lib/src/a2a/` — Agent2Agent client/server/manager (`fa serve --a2a`).
- `bin/fah.dart` + `lib/src/cli/` — the `fa` CLI: REPL, slash commands, headless/serve modes → `docs/agents/cli.md`.
- `lib/src/cube/` — fa_cube sandbox profiles → `docs/cubes.md`; `lib/src/cli/hep.dart` — HEP event protocol → `docs/hep.md`.
- `lib/src/web_search/` — `web_search` (DDG keyless → keyed providers); `tool/fa-clip/` — native macOS pasteboard helper.

**packages/ + app shells:**

- `packages/fa_ui/` — reusable widgets (incl. trajectory) → `docs/agents/fa-ui.md`; `dap_hub`, `fa_llm`, `fa_llm_mock` → `docs/dap.md`.
- `flutter_app/` — the Flutter app (desktop/mobile/web) → `docs/agents/flutter-app.md`; services one-liner: `docs/agents/services.md`; JS apps: `docs/agents/js-apps.md`; HomeKit/Calendar/CodeMie: `docs/agents/system-integrations.md`.
- `browser_ext/` + `lib/src/browser/` + `bin/serve_bridge.dart` — browser extension + WebSocket bridge → `docs/browser-extension.md`.
- `office_addin/` + FA_HOST=office app host — Office add-in → `docs/outlook-addin.md`.
- `fa_network` — external Go backend bridged via the DAP hub (channel-id caveats: `docs/dap.md` §14).
- `site/`, `scripts/`, `docs/subagents/` — landing page (privacy sync), gates + codegen, subagents master plan → `docs/agents/flutter-app-subsystems.md`.

## Hard architecture rules (stay inline)

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.
- Barrel `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart`: grouped **APPEND-ONLY** export
  sections — one `// ── <subsystem> ──` header per group, sorted by path
  within a group, new exports append to their group. No mini-barrels, no
  re-sorting (gh-1232).
- God-file ceiling: no `.dart` file over **2800** lines (crap4dart `loc`
  gate). Target < 2000 for primary files; split by concern into `part`
  files — never by extracting public API.

## Working in parallel (shared checkout + worktrees)

Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked; run no
heavy commands (full suites/analyze) in it; never `git stash` the user's
WIP; talk to peer agents through the messaging fabric, not their files.
Worktrees only if genuinely required — ask first, create detached under
`.worktrees/<name>/` from the remote tracking ref, remove when done.
Full policy: `docs/agents/parallel-worktrees.md`.

## Memory (footnote)

Before any non-trivial task, **search memory first** (`memory_search`,
then `memory_list` for fuzzy topics). Scopes: **project** = this repo
(`.fah/memory/note/` since gh-2185 — local-only, not committed; the
user's files: read freely, write only via `memory_add`), **user** = global/private. `memory_add` stores durable facts
only; supersede by delete + add — never leave solved problems to rot. The
host recomposes the `<memory>` prompt section after every add; tool wiring
is `memoryTools` + `lib/src/memory/`. Churn pitfalls: `docs/memory-churn.md`;
usage details: `docs/agents/memory-usage.md`.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done: coverage first (`test/goldens/` + `golden_guard_test.dart`
map), real fonts (`ensureGoldenFonts`), full frames (1280x800 / 390x844),
determinism, eyes on pixels after `--update-goldens`, green
`flutter test test/goldens` + `scripts/check_goldens.py` (orphan snapshots
hard-fail). Full rules: `docs/agents/golden-tests.md`.

## Prompts live outside Dart code

Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (YAML frontmatter,
`{{token}}` placeholders) — never string literals in `.dart`. After
editing: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` regenerates the `.g.dart`
files (`test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart` gates drift); Codex catalog
refresh: `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Details:
`docs/agents/prompts.md`.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The hook is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI classifies
PRs through the same script (`--dry-run`) — one classifier, one threshold
set, hook/CI parity via `GATE_STAGE` markers. Path rules: docs/markdown/
prompts-only → size + analyze; lib/bin/test/pubspec → +tests, coverage,
CRAP, dup, dupx; `test/integration/**` → +integration-mock;
flutter_app/packages → +flutter; scripts/.github → everything. Invariants:

- analyze + format clean; `dart test` green — **deterministic-only**
  (mock LLM; live models never in the gate; `llm`-tagged files run only in
  the tag-only provider smoke + nightly).
- Line coverage of `lib/` ≥ 80%; jscpd < 1% core / < 3.7% app; cross-module
  dup < 0.31%; CRAP ratchet: core 12.0, app 30.0 (thresholds only-down);
  ≤ 2800 lines per `.dart` file; AGENTS.md ceiling (top of this file).
- Red-in-≥2-distinct-SHA-runs flakes quarantine via
  `scripts/test_quarantine.json`; nightly keeps running quarantined files.

## Cross-platform parity

Every shared setting and interactive prompt type exists on BOTH the CLI
and the Flutter app unless fundamentally impossible — then it MUST be in

index f14f74b5bd..7e01e05588 100644
--- a/docs/fa_network_connector.md
+++ b/docs/fa_network_connector.md
@@ -113,6 +113,38 @@ Rules:
 - `refId` on ack/error references the delivered msgId; on
   hello_ok it references the hello.
 
+### 3.1 Client enforcement — one upstream per machine (eviction-storm fix)
+
+Incident (2026-11-25): N `fa` CLI sessions on one Mac each opened their own
+device WS under one enrolled device. The server evicts the older socket on
+every new dial, the client backoff reset on every short-lived connect and
+roster PATCHes were only debounced by 500 ms → ~100 dials/min and 500+ 429s
+per minute per machine, until the relay front refused `/ws` upgrades (phones
+lost their DM link in that storm). Client rules, pinned by
+`test/bin_network_presence_wiring_test.dart`:
+
+- `bin/` never constructs a `NetworkPresenceController`. Every CLI presence
+  site (interactive, mailbox-woken, `fa network`, the hub plugin) calls
+  `resolveCliNetworkPresence` (`lib/src/network/connector/connector_daemon_io.dart`):
+  a daemon alive for the same deviceId (state file + probe, spawned on demand)
+  yields the loopback `SharedConnectorPresenceClient` — zero upstream dials
+  from the session; without a daemon the direct controller is the fallback.
+- One-shot roster reads go through `readCliNetworkRoster`: the cached roster
+  of an alive daemon; a direct one-shot controller only when there is no
+  daemon or its cache is still empty.
+- Reconnect backoff (`ConnectorUpstreamClient`): the attempt counter resets
+  only after `upstreamStableWindow` (30 s) of uptime, equal jitter on every
+  step; a 429 on ticket mint or upgrade waits `Retry-After` when available
+  (`dart:io` exposes only the status of a refused WS upgrade → ladder
+  fallback otherwise).
+- Roster PATCH: both hosts write through one `RosterPatchLimiter` — at least
+  2 s between PATCHes per device process, `Retry-After` or a jittered
+  cooldown on 429, pending rows merged into the next flush, never dropped.
+- App: one `DeviceConnectorService` per process (`claimShared`/`release`).
+- Acceptance: `upstream_eviction_test.dart` — two clients against a
+  one-socket-per-device fake server decay from 80 to ≤ 3 dials/min per
+  client after the first minute.
+
 ## 4. Device WS protocol
 
 - Ticket: `POST /api/ws-ticket` authenticated with the **deviceToken**
@@ -261,6 +293,20 @@ not create one unbounded frame. The listing itself remains backed by the
 existing persisted listing index and bounded reads; no transcript records are
 sent.
 
+Periodic rediscovery (gh-2410) runs every 30 s (`catalogPollInterval`) through
+one shared `CatalogPoller` (`lib/src/network/connector/catalog_poller.dart`)
+in both hosts (CLI presence, connector daemon): a tick that lands while a pass
+is still running only marks it dirty and the running pass does at most ONE
+follow-up, so store passes never overlap; ticks are no-ops while the upstream
+link is not connected (nothing is published while disconnected and the next
+connect sends a full snapshot), and a reconnect refreshes exactly once so
+changes made while the link was down reach that snapshot. The store pass
+itself is stamp-cached: snippets and name probes are memoized per file under
+its (size, mtime) pair, so an unchanged store costs zero transcript reads
+(stat only) — previously every unnamed session's head/tail name windows were
+re-read on every pass, which on a 1450-file store was ~1 GiB and 13 s per
+poll, i.e. the idle-CPU burn this fixed.
+
 The roster session's existing `id`, `title`, `path`, and `lastActivity` fields
 remain the interoperability baseline. `title` is the persisted session name,
 or the bounded first-prompt snippet, or a cwd label as a final human fallback;

arguments.content:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: a zero / sub-second `Retry-After` hint bypasses the roster throttle decay**

`RosterPatchLimiter._onPatchRefused` honours the server's `Retry-After` hint
verbatim:

```dart
final delay =
    error.retryAfter ?? rosterThrottleBackoff(_throttleStreak, _jitter());
_notBefore = _clock.now().add(delay);
```

`parseRetryAfter` (rate_backoff.dart) maps `Retry-After: 0` to
`Duration.zero`, and any hint ≤ the 2 s `rosterPatchMinInterval` is swallowed
by `_waitForBudget` afterwards. So a server that keeps refusing with a
0–2 s hint keeps this limiter PATCHing at the full 2 s budget cadence
(~30 full-catalog PATCHes/min, the entire per-process budget) for as long as
the throttle lasts — the `_throttleStreak` exponential ladder
(`rosterThrottleBackoff`, cap 60 s) never engages, i.e. no decay toward the
trickle this PR's own eviction machinery establishes for dials.

The WS reconnect path in the same change already encodes the correct rule —
`upstreamRetryDelay` (upstream_client.dart:118–121):
"a throttle hint is a floor, never a shortcut"
(`if (retryAfter == null || retryAfter <= ladder) return ladder;
return retryAfter;`). The two consumers of the shared
`ConnectorThrottleSignal` disagree on hint handling; the module docs even
bill rate_backoff as "the one place … agree on what throttled means".

Suggested fix (one expression): treat a non-positive hint as absent, or take
the max with the streak ladder, e.g.

```dart
final hinted = error.retryAfter;
final delay = hinted == null || hinted <= Duration.zero
    ? rosterThrottleBackoff(_throttleStreak, _jitter())
    : hinted;
```

(or `max(hinted, rosterThrottleBackoff(...))`). Note the existing test
"429 with Retry-After is honoured verbatim" (roster_patch_limiter_test.dart:
276) uses a 7 s hint, which still wins under a `max()` floor — only the
0/sub-second case changes behavior, so a small added case
(`throttled(retryAfter: '0')` decays instead of looping) is enough.

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: Strong, well-tested incident fix (connector hardening, one-upstream routing, catalog memoization all verified green locally: 235 SDK + 33 app tests, analyze/format clean). One important robustness gap: the roster limiter honours a zero/sub-second `Retry-After` verbatim, bypassing its own decay ladder — the same hot-loop family this PR was cut to close.

**Key Issues**:
- ⚠️ `lib/src/network/connector/roster_patch_limiter.dart:250` — a `Retry-After: 0` (or ≤ 2 s) hint sustains a full-budget PATCH cadence (~30/min) under a continuous 429 with no decay; `upstreamRetryDelay` in the same PR floors the hint against the ladder ("a hint is a floor, never a shortcut") — the limiter should agree. One-expression fix; only the 0/sub-second case changes behavior.

Ranked digest (no threads — informational):
- `lib/src/cli/network_presence.dart:279` + `multi_session_connector_host.dart` — the poller's `onError` logs `'session catalog poll failed'` without the error detail, unlike every neighboring connector log (`dial failed: $error`, …); recurring background failures will be undiagnosable.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/network/network_home.dart:82` — a standalone `NetworkHomePage` claims through the bare factory; whichever surface claims first wins for the process. Today the wide shell always claims at boot, but a future earlier claimer would silently drop the full wiring — worth a line in the `claimShared` doc naming the shell as the canonical first claimer.
- `lib/src/network/connector/upstream_client.dart:249` — `start()` keeps a stale `_attempt` across a stop/start cycle (hosts are start-once today, so harmless; a reset at `start()` would make the ladder position purely link-history).
- `lib/src/cli/network_presence.dart:465` — a final retraction pending behind a throttle cooldown at `dispose()` time is dropped (`close()` cancels the retry timer); presence is best-effort and server-side no-op detection is a declared follow-up, so acceptable.

**Next Steps**:
1. Floor the roster limiter's `Retry-After` (treat ≤ 0 as absent, or max with the ladder) + add the `retryAfter: '0'` decay case.
2. Optional, non-blocking: include the error detail in the catalog-poll failure log.
